name: comp-228
title: Portrait Avatar Select
description: A dropdown for choosing one person from a short team list. Each choice shows a large round photo, a name and a handle, and the closed trigger mirrors the chosen person.
use: A form needs one teammate picked and faces plus handles make recognition faster than a plain text list.
avoid: It assumes a short fixed list; for a large directory you want a searchable combobox instead.
a11y: The label is tied to the trigger and every portrait has alt text; the open animation ignores reduced-motion settings. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark form field with a small label above it. The trigger shows a round avatar, a bold name, a grey handle and a chevron at the right. Opened, a rounded dark menu stacks three avatar rows with names and handles.
behaves: Clicking the trigger drops a list of people below it. Rows highlight under the cursor, the current choice carries a check at its right edge, and picking a row closes the menu and swaps the avatar and name on the trigger.
customise: The people, photos and handles are written in the file, so swapping them means editing the source; the label and default choice are fixed there too.
weight: light: A select with three short rows and three tiny images; nothing runs in the background.
demo: Jenny Hamilton, Paul Smith and Luna Wyen with handles such as @jennycodes.
issues: Portrait photos are low-quality placeholders and look distorted at this size.
polishWhy: Clear hierarchy and an even row rhythm; the rough portrait images drag it down.
